summary: This version of the temperature converter keeps asking until the user types a number that is both numeric and inside the valid Celsius range of -273.15 to 100, then converts it to Fahrenheit. It combines a while loop with try-catch so a bad entry no longer ends the program.

lines.text: The prompt now states the acceptable range up front, so the user knows what counts as valid before typing anything rather than discovering it through a rejection.
This loop is what lets the application keep running after a bad entry. It repeats forever until a break statement stops it, so the user gets another chance instead of having to restart the program.
Parsing succeeded, so no exception was thrown, but 200 is still not a real Celsius temperature. This is the extra validation layer that exception handling alone cannot give you.
continue jumps straight back to the top of the while loop to read another line, skipping the assignment and the break below it.
Once a value passes both checks it is stored in celsius and break ends the loop, letting the program fall through to the conversion.
Placing the catch inside the loop means non-numeric text is reported and then the loop simply asks again, rather than the whole program giving up.
